reason: The logic is right, but the change does not fit the project's memory. The equivalence holds. sky_H is always 23, 26 or 28 (sky_heights; sky_h is stored only from sky_H; sky_old_geom runs only when sky_on is set, after sky_h is stored), and L = A AND 7, so n = H-L-1 is 15 to 27. The carry is 1 on every path: after SBC sky_t, after SBC #8 (n >= 15), after each SBC #&02 (rh is &40-&7F, so rh-2-borrow >= &3D), and on the BCC fall-through and the BCS back-edge. The stores to sky_rl/rh/rt/rb/rn (bank 4 workspace &BC90-&BCAD, absolute in both versions) are the same values in the same order, with entries 1 and 2 written as the original always writes them. sky_n (&DE, sky scratch) is never read while it holds its new early value n-8. Registers at .top are the same: A = sky_n, X = the last entry, and C is not read. The problem is room. The window is &DE66-&DEAB, 69 bytes, and the new code is 133 bytes: 64 bytes larger. On this branch the shipping and bench builds end hazel_b at &DF65, so the result (&DFA5) still fits under the &E000 ASSERT. But branch gameplay-shield merges main regularly (9768fe6, 9543950, ab48579), and its HUD_RUPTURE build is the published gameplay disc, build/strykers-gameplay. That build already fills HAZEL: after sky_hazel.6502 it puts level_movers_x_low, ground_columns and rup_k_lo there (decision 67), and hazel_b_end is &DFFF, 1 byte free. The next merge of this change into gameplay-shield fails 'HAZEL overruns by' about 63 bytes, and decision 67's tables would have to be relocated. The grind's gate builds only this branch's flag sets, so it cannot catch this. Candidate 3 (1 byte smaller) or candidate 2 with its 32 bytes costed against that branch would not hit this. The cycle recount in this window, against the original 13 + 65*(k-1) + 51 for k = 2, 3, 4 entries (n 15-16, 17-24, 25-27), saves 34, 43 and 48 cycles per execution. The claimed 50.8 includes the split loop's page-crossing fixes downstream, which is plausible.
